Long, long ago, so long ago that there was no "long ago" yet, there was nothing at all: no sun, no sea, no songs of birds. There was only a quiet, quiet darkness. But that silence had, waiting just ahead, the most wonderful story in the whole world.

And then, in the darkness, a light switched on — the very first light in all the world. It spread out like a warm golden river, spilling away from the dark. And that is how day and night began: a time for playing, and a time for dreaming.
Then a great blue tent spread out above the waters — the sky. Light clouds floated across it, like little white boats. The world had become like a big, bright room, all ready for someone to move in.

Then the waters parted and gathered into seas, and up from them rose the land: hills, valleys, and tall mountains. For the very first time, the earth turned its back to the sun — and it liked how warm that felt.
And the earth turned green! Grasses and flowers grew, and trees rustled with tasty fruits: apple trees, date palms, and grapevines. The world became like one huge blooming garden.

To make the day bright and the night cozy, two little lanterns came out into the sky: a big golden sun and a silver moon. And all around the moon the stars scattered — just try to count them, you won't be able to!

Then the seas came alive. Schools of quick little fish played in the waves, crabs crawled along the seabed, and starfish swayed gently. And the biggest of all in the sea was the whale — he blew spouts of water and never, ever hurt anyone.
And up into the sky flew the birds. The big cranes flew in a line, the little birds sang on the branches, and the peacock spread his tail like a colorful fan. The sky rang with songs.

Then the animals came out onto the land: huge elephants and tall giraffes, mighty lions and swift deer, while rabbits and hedgehogs rustled through the grass. They were all neighbors, and no one was afraid of anyone.

And then the very first person appeared. His name was Adam. He was given a big job — to think up names for all the animals and birds! “You shall be an elephant, you shall be a chickadee, and you… you shall be a hedgehog.” And that’s how everyone got their very own name.

Even in a wonderful garden, it's a bit lonely all by yourself. So Adam was given a friend — Eve. Together it was much more fun: they wandered through the garden, laughed together, and got to know every flower and every animal.

Adam and Eve's home was called the Garden of Eden. It was always warm there, four rivers flowed from the garden, and fruit ripened on the trees all year round. It was the very first and the most beautiful home in the whole world.

For six days the world was made, and on the seventh day came a time of rest. Everything grew quiet: the animals dozed off, the sea grew calm, and the trees rustled softly. Ever since then, one day each week is a day of rest, to relax and be happy.

Look how nicely everything works together: the sun warms, the rain waters, the bees carry pollen, and the trees offer their fruit. Everyone in the world has their own place, and each one needs the other, like notes in a single song.

This world was entrusted to people, just as a garden is entrusted to a gardener — to cherish it and care for it. Water a little tree, don't hurt a bird, don't litter by the stream — this way, each of us carries on the very first job in the world.

And that's why, ever since, a week has had seven days — one for each day of this story. Six for work and discoveries, one for resting. That's why a day off isn't just "no school" — it's the oldest holiday in the whole world.

Now take a look out the window. The sun, the clouds, the songs of birds, a little green sprout — they're all part of that very same story. The creation of the world never really ended: every morning, the world is made new again. And in this story, you are the hero who matters most.
